name: Ivo Carnotensis
claimNotes: All three major canonical collections remain in Latin. 288 letters studied in academic publications but not translated into English.

name: Adamus Scotus (Adam of Dryburgh)
claimNotes: De tripartito tabernaculo (1180), Liber de quadripartito exercitio cellae, sermons, and theological writings—entire corpus untranslated.

name: Angelomus Luxovensis
claimNotes: Commentarius in Genesin; Enarrationes In Libros Regum; Enarrationes In Cantica Canticorum (all biblical commentaries).

name: Othlonus S. Emmerammi Ratisponensis
claimNotes: All major works—theological treatises, spiritual writings, annales—remain in Latin only.

name: Freculphus Lexovensis
claimNotes: Twelve Books of Histories (Historiarum libri XII) - major Carolingian universal chronicle - no English translation located

name: Wolbero S. Pantaleonis
claimNotes: Commentaria super Canticum Canticorum (Commentary on Song of Songs), chronicle materials

name: Hugo Rothomagensis
claimNotes: Seven works remain in Latin only

name: Joannes Belethus
claimNotes: Summa de ecclesiasticis officiis (Rationale divinorum officiorum) - German translation (Weinrich, CCT 11) but no English

name: Heterius Uxamensis
claimNotes: Adversus Elipandum libri duo (with Beatus of Liebana) - key anti-adoptionist work of 8th-c. Spain remains untranslated

name: Bandinus
claimNotes: Commentary/abridgement of Peter Lombard's Sentences (~1170) remains in Latin

name: Hildefonsus Toletanus
claimNotes: Works on baptism and theological writings remain untranslated; highly regarded in Spanish Catholic tradition

name: Folcuinus Laubiensis
claimNotes: Chronicle of Folcuin of Lobbes remains untranslated; appears in PL 137

name: Ammonius Alexandrinus
claimNotes: Grammatical works remain untranslated; ancient rather than medieval material

name: Ogerius Lucedii
claimNotes: Marian sermons and Planctus of a notable Cistercian abbot remain untranslated

name: Placidus Nonantulani
claimNotes: Glossary (medieval Latin lexical work); textual history studied but no English translation found

name: Braulio Caesaraugustanus
claimNotes: Completed works of Isidore (Etymologies in 20 books), Life of St. Emilian, hymns, letter collection; no English translation found

name: Wicbodus
claimNotes: Wigbod (8th c.): Quaestiones in Octateuchum, encyclopedic Genesis/Octateuch commentary composed for Charlemagne at Lorsch (775-800), compiled from eight Church Fathers, with prefatory hexameter poems;

name: Luculentus
claimNotes: Homiliary of Luculentius: New Testament homilies/commentary (6th-7th c., PL 72:803-860, first 18 homilies discovered by Angelo Mai); no English translation
